module.title: Unit 1: Having Fun: Present Tenses & Hobbies
module.objective: Talk about daily habits, routines, and hobbies using the Present Simple, adverbs of frequency, and verb + -ing preferences.

subModules.title: Reading Mission: Hobbies and Daily Routines
subModules.vocabularyFocus: Hobbies, Free Time Activities, and Adverbs of Frequency

content.summary: Welcome to your first reading mission. In this lesson, you will read short texts about hobbies and free-time activities. You will learn how to use the Present Simple tense to talk about daily routines and habits, and practice using verb + -ing forms to express likes and dislikes.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Present Simple affirmative, negative, and question forms, plus verb + -ing for preferences.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Words related to free time, hobbies, and frequency adverbs.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Skimming short paragraphs to get the main idea and scanning for specific details like names and activities.

learningObjectives: Understand the main idea of short A2 texts about hobbies and routines.
Locate specific details such as frequency adverbs and personal preferences.
Recognize and practice grammar patterns with Present Simple and -ing verbs.

contextWarmup.prompt: When do most teenagers usually practice their hobbies in a typical week?
options: During the weekend and after school
Before waking up in the morning
contextWarmup.explanation: Students typically have free time after school and during the weekend to enjoy their hobbies.

rules: Present Simple Affirmative: I, you, we, and they use the base verb. He, she, and it add -s or -es to the verb.
Present Simple Negative: Use don't with I, you, we, and they, and doesn't with he, she, and it before the base verb.
Present Simple Questions: Start questions with Do for I, you, we, and they, and Does for he, she, and it.
Verb + -ing for Preferences: Use verbs like like, love, hate, and enjoy followed by a verb with -ing.
Adverbs of Frequency: Place frequency words like often or occasionally before main verbs, but after the verb to be.

commonTrap.explanation: Learners often forget to add -s to the verb when talking about he, she, or it in the Present Simple tense.
commonTrap.wrong: My brother play football every Saturday.
commonTrap.correct: My brother plays football every Saturday.

content.passageTitle: Life and Hobbies of Two Teenagers
paragraphs: Hi! My name is Leo, and I am fourteen years old. I live in a busy city with my family. During the week, I go to school and study hard. In my free time, I love relaxing at home. I often play computer games with my friends online. My sister Mia does not like video games. She prefers outdoor activities and enjoys collecting rare stamps.

Mia is twelve years old. She spends her weekends visiting local markets and looking for old stamps. Occasionally, she writes a blog about her hobby to share tips with other young collectors. On Sunday evenings, our parents always ask us to tidy up our rooms before school starts again. Tidying up is never fun, but we do it anyway. Be careful when you clean your desk, Mia always says!

content.summary: This listening briefing helps you tune into natural conversations about hobbies and everyday activities. Focus on picking up key phrases used by teenagers when talking about their free time and plans.
learningObjectives: Catch the main topic of a spoken conversation about hobbies and activities.
Identify specific details such as actions, locations, and personal preferences.
Notice how words link together in fast connected speech.

keyPhrases.note: Used informally to ask what someone is currently doing or planning.
A common expression meaning to enjoy oneself during an activity.
A phrasal verb meaning to discover or learn new information.
An encouraging phrase used to urge someone to join an activity or hurry up.

connectedSpeech.note: The final /t/ in what links smoothly with are, and the /ð/ in they is elided in rapid speech.
The final consonant /d/ in find links directly to the vowel sound in out.
The final /k/ sound in look connects with at, creating a single flowing syllable.
The /d/ sound at the end of good blends into the /t/ sound of time.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Hobbies and Free Time

content.summary: Practical guide on sentence structure, present tenses, and hobby expressions in English.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Affirmative Sentences
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + Verb (-s/-es for he/she/it) + Object / Complement
blueprintItems.example: I play tennis on Saturdays and my brother plays football.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Negative Sentences
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + don't / doesn't + base verb + Object
blueprintItems.example: She doesn't like cooking dinner on weeknights.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Expressing Hobbies with -ing
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + like / love / hate / enjoy + verb-ing + Complement
blueprintItems.example: They love swimming at the community pool on Sundays.

mechanicsRules.rule: Always capitalize days of the week, months, and proper names.
mechanicsRules.why: Names of cities and days are proper nouns in English.

mechanicsRules.rule: Add -s or -es to verbs for third-person singular in affirmative present simple sentences.
mechanicsRules.why: The subject 'he' requires the verb form with an -s ending.

mechanicsRules.rule: Drop the final letter 'e' when adding -ing to verbs ending in a silent 'e'.
mechanicsRules.why: Silent 'e' is removed before adding the -ing suffix.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change the following affirmative sentence into a complete negative sentence:

targetAnswers: Luke doesn't enjoy playing video games after dinner.
Luke does not enjoy playing video games after dinner.
practicumQuestions.explanation: With third-person singular (Luke), use 'does not' or 'doesn't' followed by the base verb 'enjoy'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change the following sentence into a question:
targetAnswers: Do you play tennis on weekends?
practicumQuestions.explanation: To form a present simple question with 'you', place 'Do' at the beginning of the sentence.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Complete the sentence using the correct conjunction (and / but):
practicumQuestions.promptText: Emma likes swimming, ___ she doesn't like running.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'but' to show a contrast between two likes or dislikes.
practicumQuestions.explanation: We use 'but' to connect contrasting ideas or preferences.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence with correct capitalization and punctuation:
practicumQuestions.hint: Capitalize the name and the day of the week, and add a period.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Proper nouns like 'Anna' and 'London', as well as days like 'Monday', must be capitalized.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct -ing form of the verb in brackets:
practicumQuestions.promptText: My sister loves [cook] new recipes on Sundays.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Verbs following 'love' take the -ing form, so cook becomes cooking.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change the subject from 'I' to 'He' and adjust the verb correctly:
practicumQuestions.hint: Add an -s to the verb read for third-person singular.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Third-person singular subjects (He) require an -s ending on the present simple verb (reads).

practicumQuestions.instruction: Choose the correct linking word to complete the sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Mark plays guitar ___ sings in a band.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'and' to add similar activities together.
practicumQuestions.explanation: We use 'and' to link two related actions or hobbies.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Fix the spelling error in the -ing verb in this sentence:

targetAnswers: They like writing stories in their free time.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Verbs ending in a silent 'e' drop the 'e' before adding -ing.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Put the adverb of frequency in the correct position within the sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: I [always] listen to music in the morning.
targetAnswers: I always listen to music in the morning.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Adverbs of frequency like 'always' are placed before the main verb in present simple sentences.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change the following negative sentence into an affirmative sentence:

practicumQuestions.hint: Remove 'doesn't' and add 's' to the verb 'play'.
practicumQuestions.explanation: To make a third-person singular sentence affirmative, remove auxiliary 'does not' and add '-s' to the main verb.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Hobbies and Free Time

content.summary: Learn how to talk about your hobbies and daily routines using the Present Simple tense and -ing forms clearly and naturally at an A2 level.
content.audioGuidance: Focus on sentence stress, linking words, and clear vowel sounds when speaking about your free time.

pillars.name: Vowel Clarity
pillars.explanation: Pronounce short vowels like in hobby and long vowels like in relax with distinct mouth shapes.

pillars.name: Sentence Stress
pillars.explanation: Stress main verbs and nouns such as collect, blog, and weekend to make your speech easy to understand.

pillars.name: Intonation
pillars.explanation: Use a rising tone for asking questions and a falling tone when giving clear answers about your daily habits.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Notice that the main stress stays on the second syllable.
The stress remains firmly on the first syllable in both singular and plural forms.
The stress shifts slightly to the middle syllable when changing from verb to noun.
Adding the adverb ending moves the primary stress to the fourth syllable.

drills.targetText: I usually hang out with my classmates after school.
drills.phonetic: /aɪ ˈjuːʒuəli hæŋ aʊt wɪð maɪ ˈklɑːsmeɪts ˈɑːftə skuːl/
drills.focus: Phrasal verb hang out and natural rhythm
drills.hint: Link hang and out smoothly together.

drills.targetText: Do you like collecting old stamps in your free time?
drills.phonetic: /duː juː laɪk kəˈlektɪŋ əʊld stæmps ɪn jɔː friː taɪm/
drills.focus: Verb plus ing form and question intonation
drills.hint: Raise your voice slightly at the end of the question.

drills.targetText: She occasionally writes a blog about her weekend hobbies.
drills.phonetic: /ʃiː əˈkeɪʒnəli raɪts ə blɒɡ əˈbaʊt hɜː ˈwiːkend ˈhɒbiːz/
drills.focus: Third person singular verb ending and adverbs
drills.hint: Pronounce the final s in writes and relaxes clearly.

drills.targetText: Be careful when you tidy up your room today.
drills.phonetic: /bi ˈkeəfəl wen juː ˈtaɪdi ʌp jɔː ruːm təˈdeɪ/
drills.focus: Warning phrase and phrasal verb stress
drills.hint: Stress the word careful and tidy up clearly.
